A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfoTok work and support reliable comparison of text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The new Appendix A in v3 shifts the earlier Appendices A-D to B-E; their retained content can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments on TokenBench and DAVIS, routing and compressor ablations, and resolution and inference-latency results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds frame-level reconstructions, token masks, and token-usage outcomes in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The ELBO-based router, likelihood-based token selection, transformer compressor/decompressor, training objective, and InfoTok-Flex procedure are unchanged. The new illustrations demonstrate the existing method.

E1.justification: Training coverage, TokenBench and DAVIS reconstruction evaluation, and the additional resolution scenarios are retained. The dog and workshop illustrations remain within the existing video-reconstruction coverage and introduce no distinct task or domain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including Open-MAGVIT2-UCF, OmniTokenizer, Cosmos-DV4x8x8, ElasticTok, optimal routing, and the masking alternatives. The new appendix illustrations show InfoTok without adding a comparator.

E3.justification: The stated splits, cropping, reconstruction metrics, BPP16 settings, training configuration, 33-frame inference procedure, and latency-testing conditions are unchanged. The added illustrations do not report a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix A adds two qualitative case studies examining how spatial token masks and token usage vary as dog and workshop scenes change over time. Existing router, compressor, architecture, compression-rate, and resolution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The added illustrations introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 5-6 add frame-level reconstruction, mask, and token-usage results. For example, Figure 6 reports 65%, 50%, 29%, and 17% usage at frames 0, 20, 40, and 60. Existing numerical results in Tables 1-3 and 5-6 and the curves in Figure 4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorems, equations, and proofs are retained. The proofs move from Appendix A to Appendix B with pagination changes, without substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about inefficient data-agnostic routing, near-optimal information-based allocation, and improved compression and inference efficiency. The new examples do not redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: The new figure captions interpret masked ground and peripheral workshop regions as predictable from surrounding areas or previous frames, connecting these patterns to reduced token requirements. The applicability discussion and limitations in Section 6 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Architecture settings in Table 4, hyperparameters, hardware, training time, EMA implementation, and inference details are retained as Appendix B becomes Appendix C. The code-link destination is unchanged despite revised footnote wording.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against previous fixed-length and adaptive tokenizers remain unchanged. Changed bibliography back-references reflect the new pagination.

P1.justification: v3 adds a contents page and illustration appendix, updates appendix references, revises the Figure 1 caption, and makes limited grammar and footnote edits, including an oral-acceptance note. The main narrative and existing section order are largely retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 5-6 with original frames, reconstructions, binary masks, and token-usage bars, plus a contents-page layout. Figure 1's caption changes, while existing figure graphics and table structures are retained; the earlier appendices shift and partially reflow.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's reconstruction examples, v3's Figures 5-6 make token allocation over space and time directly inspectable, adding useful qualitative support. The contents page also improves navigation. These are limited gains because the method, theoretical and benchmark evidence, reproducibility details, and stated limitations remain unchanged.
